faculty_override_note: The official two-year, four-semester map is the default. The official five-semester map is an alternate lighter-load pathway. DegreeWorks and faculty advisement remain authoritative.
sequence_notes: MAT 206 is required and satisfies the Mathematical and Quantitative Reasoning Common Core area; speak to an advisor about the appropriate math pathway.
MAT 301 requires MAT 206. MAT 209 requires MAT 206 or MAT 206.5.
Students must be eligible to take MAT 206 in order to take ECO 202; this placement rule is not modeled as a course prerequisite.
Students who use ECO 201 and/or ECO 202 to satisfy a Flexible Core requirement may substitute a general elective instead.
SOC 100 is BMCC's strongly encouraged default for Individual and Society; the full Pathways pool remains available.
POL 100 is BMCC's strongly encouraged default for one of the two U.S. Experience in Its Diversity courses; the full Pathways pool remains available for both slots.
PSY 100 is BMCC's strongly encouraged default for Scientific World; PHY 110 is listed as the alternate for the Life and Physical Sciences area (AST 110 is the shown default).
SPE 102 is the listed alternate to SPE 100 for non-native speakers of English.
The History requirement accepts any History course, or one course from ANT, GEO, PHI, POL, PSY, or SOC.
A total of 3 upper-level Economics electives (9 credits) are required. ECO 201 and ECO 202 cannot be used to satisfy this requirement.

The published 4-credit General Elective requirement is satisfied by 2 explicit credits plus 2 credits of excess STEM-variant Common Core credit generated by MAT 206 and AST 110/PHY 110 each being 4-credit courses in nominally 3-credit Common Core areas.
A Writing Intensive course is required for graduation.
